//providerReviewerAllowlist: Who may satisfy the cross-review, deliberately separate from the author list. It holds agent identities only: a human approval is a human approval, never a substitute for the counter provider's review.
//reviewModeLabels: Set by the user, never by an agent: they decide who reviews the current head. The reconciler only removes one that was bound to an earlier head, so the choice is asked again per head SHA.
//statusCommentAuthors: Identities whose status comment may carry the review-mode binding. Narrower than the trusted-author check used to adopt a comment, because that one accepts every [bot] login and the binding decides whether an answer counts for this head.
//sensitivePathPrefixes: Paths that always make the recommendation fall back to the independent cross-review, regardless of how small the diff looks.
//crossReviewEvidence: What proves the counter provider reviewed the current head. `approval` demands an approving review — the strongest signal, but the Codex integration never submits one: it comments when it has suggestions and reacts with a thumbs-up when it has none, so this value leaves `cross` permanently unsatisfiable. `reviewed-and-resolved` accepts a review of this exact head with none of its findings left open; weaker, because it infers agreement from an absence instead of reading a statement. An explicit CHANGES_REQUESTED blocks under both.
//selfReviewMinimumEnforcement: How strongly a self-review session must have been kept away from the code before its verdict opens the gate. `true` requires credentials without code write access — the strongest, but unreachable in environments whose only credentials can push. `verified` accepts a session the launcher ran with the editing tools removed in a throwaway worktree and checked afterwards to be untouched. `false` accepts a verdict nothing outside the prompt backed up and effectively turns the self-review gate into a formality.
